content.thinking: I've confirmed that PA1492 moved from its own isolated fold (c.137) in SCOP 1.69 to being classified as a probable homolog of nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase within superfamily c.23.14 by SCOPe 2.08, with the reclassification occurring at SCOP 1.71 and persisting since. I now have everything needed to answer the question.

answers.answer:
The current SCOPe release is 2.08 (frozen 2021-07-28, latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16).

SCOP 1.69: PA1492 from Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PDB 1t1j; domains d1t1ja_ and d1t1jb_, sunids 106249 and 106250) was classified as a singleton lineage of its own: fold c.137 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110459), superfamily c.137.1 (sunid 110460), family c.137.1.1 (sunid 110461), protein 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110462). Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase from Lactobacillus leichmannii (PDB 1f8y; d1f8ya_ and d1f8yb_, sunids 31395 and 31396) was in the flavodoxin-like fold c.23 (sunid 52171), superfamily c.23.14 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' (sunid 52309), family c.23.14.1, protein sunid 52311. In 1.69 the two proteins therefore shared only the class level (c, alpha/beta proteins): SCOP asserted neither a common fold nor any evolutionary relationship between them.

Current SCOPe 2.08: PA1492 has been moved out of its own fold and into the flavodoxin-like fold c.23, superfamily c.23.14, which was renamed 'N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like' (same sunid 52309). PA1492 forms its own family c.23.14.2 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (family sunid 110461 retained, protein sunid 110462; domains d1t1ja1 A:1-118 and d1t1jb1 B:1-118, with the N-terminal tag residues split off as class l.1.1.1 artifact domains d1t1ja2/d1t1jb2). 1f8y remains in family c.23.14.1 'Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase'. The old fold c.137 and superfamily c.137.1 no longer exist.

So the relationship changed from 'same class only, unrelated folds' (1.69) to 'same fold and same superfamily, different families' (2.08). This is exactly the kind of case Andreeva et al. 2008 cite: a structural-genomics protein of unknown function (MCSG target APC5043) initially given a new fold, then recognized as a remote homolog of the N-deoxyribosyltransferases and merged into their superfamily. The API shows the move already in SCOP 1.71 (c.23.14.2) and it persists through 1.73, 1.75 and all SCOPe releases to 2.08.

Evolutionary strength and limits: superfamily membership means SCOP/SCOPe curators judged PA1492 and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase to be probable homologs on the basis of structural and functional-site similarity, not detectable sequence similarity; placement in separate families (c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1) means they are not considered close relatives with clear sequence-level similarity. The 1.69 fold-level separation was a curator judgment later revised, illustrating that fold/superfamily assignments for singleton structural-genomics proteins are provisional and release-dependent. Being in the same superfamily does not license transferring the specific nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase enzymatic function to PA1492 (SCOPe still labels it 'Hypothetical protein'); any functional inference would need independent biochemical evidence, and 1f8y should be used as a structural template for PA1492 only as a remote-homology (superfamily-level) template with expected low sequence identity. Note also that sunids for the domains, protein and family (106249, 106250, 110462, 110461) were kept stable across the move, so the reclassification is visible by comparing the sccs of the same sunid across releases, whereas the old fold and superfamily sunids (110459, 110460) were retired.
evidence_used: Pretrained knowledge: Andreeva et al. 2008 NAR SCOP 1.73/1.75 paper describing PA1492 as a reclassification example
